page.layout: One printed page (left-hand text column, cut off at the left edge of the scan), with running head "LIBER I." and page number 525 at top right; a diagram (armillary-style circle of the globe with labels) in the middle; caption notes beneath the diagram; and a closing catchword-like line "Restat" at lower right.

main_text.p: cius Episcopus Moguntinus Virgilium Episcopum Salisburgensem tanquam hæreticum accusarit coram Pontifice Rom. Zacharia propterea quod Virgilius statue-ret, reuera dari Antipodes. Re tandem ad Bohemorum regem delata & deinde ad Pontificem appellatione facta Virgilius propter antipodes hæreseos damnatus est. Vsque adeo magna vis inest bonorum studiorum ignorantiæ etiam ad excarnificandas hominum conscientias. Vide de hac historia Auentinum autorem fide dignissimum lib.3. h'storiæ Bauaricæ. Cæterum qui plura volet de illa quæstione, an sint antipodes, legat Commentar. 1. de cœlo c.14 quæstione 2, artic.4. vbi omnia contraria argumenta diluuntur. Addat etiam Lucillum Philalthæum super textum Aristotelis 18. lib.2. de cœlo.
β. Æquator vel potius eius diameter. γ, δ. Poli mundi.
ABCD Circulus Meridianus. Vide Mich. Mestlinum in Epitome Astronom.

page.notes: The diagram shows a meridian circle with labels: Polus Arcticus, Polus antarcticus, Periœci, Antœci, Antipodes, Podes, Meridianus, Coluris (partly cut off), points A, B, C, D, α, β, γ, δ. The left portion of the text is cut off by the scan edge; the first line is a fragment. Some words in the diagram are garbled in print and are transcribed as printed.
